newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ninety-five countries back milestone landmine ban.
newsitem.headline: Ninety-five countries back milestone landmine ban.

text.p: Ninety-five countries have expressed their support for a first ever international landmine ban treaty, to be signed in Ottawa in December, officials at a Brussels conference on the ban told Reuters on Friday.
The countries have signed the so-called Brussels Declaration which will form the basis for negotiations in Oslo in September on the exact wording of the Ottawa treaty.

"This is a milestone on the road to a complete ban," Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke told the conference, adding: "It is too early to cry victory, we have to wait for the final signing in Ottawa."

"Brussels has shown there is no way back and that the world community stands behind a total ban on landmines. Some countries are not willing yet to ban mines. I think they are ill-advised. I call upon all the countries which have not signed the declaration to join this movement and ban these dreadlful weapons," Derycke said.
A total of 115 countries took part in the Brussels talks to prepare the way for a ban of the production, use, stockpiling and transfer of anti-personnel landmines.
The United States, which is attending the conference as an observer only, will not sign because it favours separate United Nations-sponsored landmine talks in Geneva.

Some of the 36 other countries which took part as observers also prefer the Geneva conference. They included Cuba, India, Indonesia, Iran, Israel, Libya, Pakistan, the Palestinian Authority and Turkey.
